source_text:
Ὅθεν πρέπει ὑμῖν συντρέχειν τῇ τοῦ ἐπισκόπου γνώμῃ, ὅπερ καὶ ποιεῖτε. τὸ γὰρ ἀξιονόμαστον ὑμῶν πρεσβυτέριον, τοῦ θεοῦ ἄξιον, οὕτως συνήρμοσται τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ, ὡς χορδαὶ κιθάρᾳ. διὰ τοῦτο ἐν τῇ ὁμονοίᾳ ὑμῶν καὶ συμφώνῳ ἀγάπῃ Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ᾅδεται.
καὶ οἱ κατ’ ἄνδρα δὲ χορὸς γίνεσθε, ἵνα σύμφωνοι ὄντες ἐν ὁμονοίᾳ, χρῶμα θεοῦ λαβόντες ἐν ἑνότητι, ᾅδητε ἐν φωνῇ μιᾷ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τῷ πατρί, ἵνα ὑμῶν καὶ ἀκούσῃ καὶ ἐπιγινώσκῃ, δἰ ὦν εὖ πράσσετε, μέλη ὄντας τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ. χρήσιμον οὖν ἐστὶν ὑμᾶς ἐν ἀμώμῳ ἑνότητι εἶναι, ἵνα καὶ θεοῦ πάντοτε μετέχητε.
thought_title: Harmony with the bishop as strings of a lyre
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Ephesus, urging them to align with their bishop Onesimus and the council of elders.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore it is fitting for you to run together with the mind of the bishop, which indeed you also do. For your council of elders, worthy of its name, worthy of God, has been fitted together with the bishop as strings to a lyre. Because of this, in your concord and harmonious love, Jesus Christ is sung. And you also become a chorus man by man, so that being harmonious in concord, having received the stamp of God in unity, you may sing in one voice through Jesus Christ to the Father, so that he may both hear you and recognize you, through the things you do well, as being members of his Son. It is useful therefore for you to be in blameless unity, so that you may also always partake of God.

lemmas.gloss: to run together with, to align with
to be fitted together, joined together

choices.english: to run together with the mind of the bishop
choices.why: Keeps the literal metaphor of running together, which conveys active alignment rather than passive agreement
rejected: to agree with the bishop's opinion

choices.why: Preserves the compound adjective literally, emphasizing the honor of the council of elders

choices.term: συνήρμοσται τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ, ὡς χορδαὶ κιθάρᾳ
choices.english: has been fitted together with the bishop as strings to a lyre
choices.why: Keeps the musical image exact: strings are fitted to the lyre, not the reverse
rejected: is joined to the bishop like strings on a harp
is attuned to the bishop as strings to a guitar

choices.english: having received the color of God
choices.why: Retains the unusual musical metaphor of 'color' as tone or timbre, which is lost if paraphrased
Keeps the adjective 'blameless' modifying unity, which is the literal force

choices.english: as being members of his Son
choices.why: Preserves the participial clause and the body metaphor exactly
rejected: since you are limbs of his Son

pass_b_english: So you must align yourselves with the mind of the bishop, as you are already doing. Your council of elders, worthy of its name and worthy of God, is fitted together with the bishop as strings are fitted to a lyre. Because of this, in your concord and harmonious love, Jesus Christ is sung.

And let each of you become a choir, so that being in harmony and concord, having received the tuning of God in unity, you may sing with one voice through Jesus Christ to the Father, so that the Father may both hear you and recognize you, through the good you do, as members of his Son. It is useful, then, for you to be in blameless unity, so that you may always share in God.

last_rejected.why: 'Must' is too strong; πρέπει means 'it is fitting/proper', not necessity. Changes tone from fitting to obligation.
last_rejected.fix: So it is fitting for you to run together with
last_rejected.ruling: πρέπει means 'it is fitting/necessary'; 'must' is within normal range and not a meaning change.

last_rejected.why: 'Useful' understates χρήσιμον; 'beneficial' or 'profitable' better, but 'useful' is within range. No error.
last_rejected.ruling: Claim itself admits 'useful' is within range of χρήσιμον; no error.

problems.quote: having received the color of God in unity
problems.why: 'Color' is odd; may mean 'character' (Greek 'chroma' as variant for 'charakter') or 'complexion'.
Same office rendered two ways; readers may think 'elders' are different from 'council of elders.'
Same underlying metaphor (charakter/stamp/imprint) rendered differently; reader misses the connection.
problems.fix: Use 'stamp' or 'imprint' consistently for this metaphor.

edits.new: having received the character of God in unity

fixed: The glossary issue about 'council of elders' is not a problem in this passage: the English consistently uses 'council of elders' for πρεσβυτέριον, and no other rendering of the same office appears here.
The glossary issue about 'character of God' is addressed by the edit changing 'color' to 'character', which matches the metaphor consistently in this passage.

problems.why: Same office rendered two ways; readers may miss the equivalence.
problems.fix: Use 'council of elders (presbyters)' at first occurrence.

problems.fix: Use consistent 'council of elders' with note.

problems.why: Same word 'council' used for presbyterion and apostolic group, but different Greek words may be involved; still risks conflation.
problems.fix: Note Greek terms or use 'college of apostles' if distinct.

problems.why: Same office rendered two ways; readers may think presbyters are a different group.

The gloss now matches the English wording for the phrase, avoiding the inconsistent parenthetical.
The second and third reported problems refer to a different passage not present in this section; no change needed here.

problems.why: 'Character' in 1.4 ('received the character of God in unity') and 'stamp' in 2.5-6 translate the same Greek concept; reader may miss connection.
problems.fix: Use 'stamp' or 'mark' consistently; gloss 'character' if retained.

problems.quote: having received the character of God in unity, you may sing with one voice through Jesus Christ to the Father, so that he may both hear you and recognize you, through the good you do, as members of his Son.
problems.why: Antecedent of 'he' shifts from Father to Son awkwardly; 'members of his Son' is odd phrasing.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'so that the Father may both hear you and recognize you, through the good you do, as members of his Son.'

problems.why: Same body rendered three ways; reader may miss they are identical.
problems.fix: Use 'council of elders' consistently; gloss others as metaphors.

The 'character' vs 'stamp' issue is addressed by changing the gloss to 'stamp' to match the other passage, while the English retains 'character' as a natural rendering.

problems.why: Same Greek word (presbyterion) rendered as 'council of elders' but also 'council of the bishop' and 'council of the apostles', which may confuse readers about whether these are the same body.
problems.fix: Use 'council of elders' consistently; note 'council of the apostles' is a different metaphor.

problems.why: In 2.6, elders stand 'in the place of the council of the apostles'—but 'council of the apostles' is not the same as 'council of elders', though both use 'council'. Reader may conflate them.
problems.fix: Clarify that 'council of the apostles' is a separate metaphor for the apostolic college.

problems.why: Unique phrase 'council of the bishop' in 5.8; elsewhere always 'council of elders'. Reader may wonder if this is a different body or a mistake.
problems.fix: Verify Greek; likely should be 'council of elders' or add note explaining this variant.

problems.quote: having received the stamp of God in unity
problems.why: 'Stamp' (Greek: charagma) usually means mark/imprint, but here likely 'tuning' or 'harmony'; context is musical.
problems.fix: Revise to 'having received God's tuning in unity' or add note.

problems.why: Same office rendered four ways; 'council of God' and 'council of the bishop' could be mistaken for different bodies.
problems.fix: Use 'council of elders' consistently; reserve 'apostles' for the apostles.

council of elders: The English correctly renders πρεσβυτέριον as 'council of elders' per the glossary. No edit needed.
